epj-c1-t01.title: JDBC
epj-c1-t01.definition: JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) is a Java API that lets Java programs connect to relational databases, execute SQL statements and process the results.
epj-c1-t01.simpleExplanation: JDBC Java ko database se baat karne ka standard tareeka hai. Connection banao, SQL bhejo, ResultSet padho, aur sab close karo.
epj-c1-t01.realLifeAnalogy: JDBC is like a universal phone adaptor: your Java code speaks one standard language and the driver translates it for each database.
epj-c1-t01.example: Connect to MySQL, run SELECT and print rows (see code). Steps: load driver → get Connection → create Statement → execute query → process ResultSet → close.
keyPoints: Package java.sql; part of Java SE.
Five steps: load driver, establish connection, create statement, execute, close.
Statement vs PreparedStatement (precompiled, prevents SQL injection) vs CallableStatement (stored procedures).
executeQuery for SELECT; executeUpdate for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.

examQuestions.question: Explain JDBC and its steps.
examQuestions.answer: Define; list five steps with code.

examQuestions.question: Statement vs PreparedStatement.
examQuestions.answer: Statement compiles each time and is injection-prone; PreparedStatement is precompiled with ? parameters and safer.

examQuestions.question: Which method for UPDATE queries?
examQuestions.answer: executeUpdate().

knowledgeCheck.question: Statement vs CallableStatement.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Statement runs plain SQL; CallableStatement calls stored procedures.

epj-c1-t01.quickRevision: JDBC: java.sql; driver → Connection → Statement/PreparedStatement → ResultSet → close; executeQuery vs executeUpdate.
epj-c1-t01.codeExplanation: DriverManager creates the Connection; try-with-resources closes it; executeQuery returns rows; rs.next() moves to each row.
commonErrors: ClassNotFoundException/No suitable driver: connector JAR missing.
Communications link failure — DB not running or wrong URL/port.

epj-c1-t02.title: JDBC Architecture
epj-c1-t02.definition: JDBC architecture has an application layer using the JDBC API, a Driver Manager that selects a driver, and JDBC drivers (Type 1–4) that talk to the database, supporting two-tier and three-tier models.
epj-c1-t02.simpleExplanation: JDBC architecture: Java app → JDBC API → DriverManager → JDBC driver → Database. Driver ke 4 types hote hain; Type 4 (pure Java) sabse zyada use hota hai.
epj-c1-t02.realLifeAnalogy: A translator chain: you speak to the interpreter (API), who selects the right translator (driver), who talks to the foreigner (database).
epj-c1-t02.example: Application calls DriverManager.getConnection(url); DriverManager picks a registered driver matching the URL, which opens the connection to MySQL.
keyPoints: Layers: JDBC API, DriverManager/DataSource, JDBC driver, database.
Two-tier: client app talks directly to DB; three-tier: app → application server → DB.
Type 4: Thin pure-Java driver (most common; e.g. MySQL Connector/J).
commonMistakes: Mixing the driver JAR version with the DB version.

examQuestions.question: Explain JDBC architecture and driver types.
examQuestions.answer: Layers and four types with pros/cons.

examQuestions.question: Type 2 vs Type 4 driver.
examQuestions.answer: Type 2 needs native libraries; Type 4 is pure Java and platform independent.

knowledgeCheck.question: JDBC-ODBC bridge is a Type 1 driver.
Three-tier app: where does JDBC run?
Two-tier vs three-tier.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Two-tier: client → DB; three-tier: client → app server → DB.

epj-c1-t02.quickRevision: JDBC arch: App → JDBC API → DriverManager → Driver (Type 1–4) → DB; Type 4 = pure Java thin driver.
epj-c1-t02.codeExplanation: The URL prefix jdbc:mysql tells DriverManager to use the MySQL Type 4 driver; metadata shows the driver in use.
commonErrors: No suitable driver found for jdbc:... (wrong URL or missing JAR).

epj-c1-t03.title: JDBC with Oracle and MySQL
epj-c1-t03.definition: Connecting JDBC to Oracle and MySQL requires the respective driver JARs, driver class names and URLs; the rest of the JDBC code stays the same.
epj-c1-t03.simpleExplanation: Oracle aur MySQL ke liye alag driver JAR, driver class aur URL chahiye. Baaki JDBC code same rehta hai.
epj-c1-t03.realLifeAnalogy: The same TV remote logic, but you load the right batteries and codes for each brand.
epj-c1-t03.example: MySQL: URL jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/college, driver com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver. Oracle: URL jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:xe, driver oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver (ojdbc JAR). Insert a row with PreparedStatement.
keyPoints: MySQL driver: mysql-connector-j JAR; class com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver; port 3306.
Oracle driver: ojdbc JAR; class oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver; port 1521; SID/service name.
Differences: SQL dialect, auto-increment (MySQL) vs sequences (Oracle), LIMIT vs ROWNUM/FETCH.
commonMistakes: Wrong URL format for Oracle (SID vs service).
Missing JAR in the classpath/Maven dependency.

examQuestions.question: Write JDBC code to insert a record in MySQL.
examQuestions.answer: PreparedStatement with ? placeholders and executeUpdate.

examQuestions.question: MySQL vs Oracle JDBC setup.
examQuestions.answer: URL, driver class, port, JAR and SQL dialect differ.

examQuestions.question: Is Class.forName required?
examQuestions.answer: Not since JDBC 4.0 (drivers auto-register).

knowledgeCheck.question: 'No suitable driver' error. Fix?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Add the correct driver JAR and verify the URL.

knowledgeCheck.question: MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT vs Oracle?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Oracle uses sequences (or identity columns in newer versions).

epj-c1-t03.quickRevision: JDBC MySQL: com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver, jdbc:mysql://host:3306/db; Oracle: oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver, jdbc:oracle:thin:@host:1521:xe.
epj-c1-t03.codeExplanation: Placeholders ? are filled by setInt/setString; executeUpdate returns the number of rows affected.
commonErrors: ORA-12505 / listener errors: wrong SID or service name.
Forgetting to commit when auto-commit is off.

epj-c1-t04.title: Maven: Integration with Eclipse
epj-c1-t04.definition: Maven is a build and dependency-management tool that uses a standard project structure and the POM file; Eclipse integrates it through the m2e plugin to create, build and run Maven projects.
epj-c1-t04.simpleExplanation: Maven dependencies (JAR) automatic download karta hai aur project build karta hai. Eclipse me m2e plugin se Maven project banate hain: File → New → Maven Project.
epj-c1-t04.realLifeAnalogy: A project manager who orders all the libraries you need, builds your project in a standard way, and keeps everything organised.
epj-c1-t04.example: Eclipse: File → New → Maven Project → archetype maven-archetype-quickstart → groupId com.college, artifactId demo → Finish. Add dependency in pom.xml; Run As → Maven build… goals: clean install.
keyPoints: Standard layout: src/main/java, src/main/resources, src/test/java, pom.xml, target/.
Local repository ~/.m2/repository; central repository downloads JARs.
Lifecycle phases: validate, compile, test, package, verify, install, deploy.
Common goals: clean, compile, test, package, install.
Eclipse m2e: Maven → Update Project after editing pom.xml.
commonMistakes: Not running Update Project after changing pom.xml.

examQuestions.question: Explain Maven and its integration with Eclipse.
examQuestions.answer: Features, layout, lifecycle, m2e steps.

examQuestions.question: mvn clean vs mvn install.
examQuestions.answer: clean deletes target; install builds, tests and copies artifact to local repository.

knowledgeCheck.question: JAR not found after editing pom. Action?
Maven vs Ant.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Maven uses conventions and dependency management; Ant is script-based.

epj-c1-t04.quickRevision: Maven: standard layout, pom.xml, lifecycle (compile/test/package/install), ~/.m2; Eclipse m2e: New Maven Project, Update Project.
epj-c1-t04.code:
mvn archetype:generate -DgroupId=com.college -DartifactId=demo -DarchetypeArtifactId=maven-archetype-quickstart -DinteractiveMode=false
cd demo
mvn clean install
epj-c1-t04.codeExplanation: The archetype creates the standard layout; clean install compiles, tests, packages the JAR and installs it in ~/.m2.

epj-c1-t05.title: POM.xml
epj-c1-t05.definition: pom.xml (Project Object Model) is the Maven configuration file that defines project coordinates, dependencies, properties, build plugins and packaging.
epj-c1-t05.simpleExplanation: pom.xml Maven ka dil hai: project ka naam (groupId, artifactId, version), kaunsi libraries chahiye (dependencies), kaise build karna hai (plugins), aur packaging (jar/war).
epj-c1-t05.realLifeAnalogy: The shopping list and recipe card of the project: what to buy and how to cook.
epj-c1-t05.example: A pom with MySQL connector as dependency and servlet-api as provided scope, packaging war (see code).
commonMistakes: Using compile scope for servlet-api (conflicts with Tomcat).

examQuestions.question: Write a pom.xml with MySQL and Servlet dependencies.
examQuestions.answer: XML below.

examQuestions.question: What is 'provided' scope?
examQuestions.answer: Needed at compile time but supplied by the runtime container (e.g. servlet API).

knowledgeCheck.question: Servlet API supplied by Tomcat. Scope?
runtime vs test scope.
knowledgeCheck.answer: runtime: needed to run, not compile; test: only for tests.

epj-c1-t05.quickRevision: pom.xml: groupId/artifactId/version, dependencies (+scope), properties, plugins, packaging.
epj-c1-t05.codeExplanation: Coordinates identify the artifact; dependencies are fetched; servlet-api is provided by Tomcat; packaging war creates a deployable WAR.
commonErrors: Version typo causing 'Could not resolve dependencies'.

epj-c2-t01.title: Basics of Web
epj-c2-t01.definition: Web basics cover the client–server model, HTTP request/response, URLs, static vs dynamic content and the role of a web container such as Tomcat that runs servlets.
epj-c2-t01.simpleExplanation: Web me browser (client) request bhejta hai, server response deta hai (HTTP). Static page fixed hota hai, dynamic page servlets/JSP se banta hai. Tomcat jaisa web container servlets chalata hai.
epj-c2-t01.realLifeAnalogy: A restaurant: customer (browser) places an order (request), the kitchen (server) prepares and serves (response).
epj-c2-t01.example: Browser sends GET /hello HTTP/1.1; Tomcat routes it to HelloServlet; servlet writes HTML; response 200 OK is returned.
keyPoints: Methods: GET (retrieve, parameters in URL), POST (submit, body), PUT, DELETE.
Status codes: 200 OK, 302 redirect, 400, 403, 404 not found, 500 server error.
Static content: HTML; dynamic: servlets, JSP.
Web container: manages servlet lifecycle (Tomcat, Jetty).
commonMistakes: Putting sensitive data in GET URLs.

examQuestions.question: GET vs POST.
examQuestions.answer: GET: data in URL, bookmarkable, limited, idempotent; POST: data in body, secure-ish, no size limit.

examQuestions.question: Explain basics of web application architecture.
examQuestions.answer: Client–server, HTTP, container, WAR.

knowledgeCheck.question: Login form should hide password in URL. Method?
Static vs dynamic content.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Static is fixed files; dynamic is generated per request.

epj-c2-t01.quickRevision: Web: client–server over HTTP (stateless); GET/POST; 200/302/404/500; Tomcat container; WAR with WEB-INF.
epj-c2-t01.code:
GET /app/hello?name=Asha HTTP/1.1 Host: localhost:8080 HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html

Hello Asha
epj-c2-t01.codeExplanation: Request line has method, path with query string and version; the response has a status line, headers and body.

epj-c2-t02.title: Servlet Lifecycle
epj-c2-t02.definition: The servlet lifecycle is managed by the container: loading and instantiation, init() once, service() for each request (doGet/doPost) and destroy() once before unloading.
epj-c2-t02.simpleExplanation: Servlet ki life: container class load karke object banata hai, init() ek baar chalata hai, har request par service() (jo doGet/doPost bulata hai), aur band hone par destroy().
epj-c2-t02.realLifeAnalogy: A shop employee: hired and trained once (init), serves many customers (service), and is released at closing (destroy).
epj-c2-t02.example: A servlet printing messages in init, doGet and destroy shows the order: init → doGet (per request) → destroy.
keyPoints: Phases: loading, instantiation, init(ServletConfig), service(), destroy().
init() and destroy() are called once; service() per request.
One servlet instance serves many requests using multiple threads.
service() dispatches to doGet/doPost based on HTTP method.
Instance variables are shared among threads → not thread safe.
load-on-startup loads the servlet at server start.
commonMistakes: Using instance variables to store per-user data.
Overriding service() unintentionally and breaking doGet/doPost.

examQuestions.question: Explain the servlet lifecycle with a diagram.
examQuestions.answer: Load → init → service(doGet/doPost) → destroy.

examQuestions.question: How many instances of a servlet exist?
examQuestions.answer: One per declaration; requests are served by multiple threads.

knowledgeCheck.question: service() is called for every request.
Counter field incremented in doGet gives wrong values under load. Reason?
init vs constructor.
knowledgeCheck.answer: init receives ServletConfig and is the lifecycle initialiser; constructor lacks container context.

epj-c2-t02.quickRevision: Lifecycle: load/instantiate → init() once → service()→doGet/doPost per request → destroy() once; single instance, many threads.
epj-c2-t02.expectedOutput: Console: init, doGet (for each request), destroy (on shutdown)
epj-c2-t02.codeExplanation: init runs once at first use; each browser hit runs doGet; destroy runs when the app stops.

epj-c2-t03.title: Servlets API
epj-c2-t03.definition: The Servlet API consists of the javax.servlet and javax.servlet.http packages (jakarta.servlet in newer versions) that define Servlet, ServletConfig, ServletContext, request/response, HttpServlet and HttpSession.
epj-c2-t03.simpleExplanation: Servlet API me interfaces aur classes hain: Servlet → GenericServlet → HttpServlet. Request se data padhte hain, response me output likhte hain.
epj-c2-t03.realLifeAnalogy: The standard toolkit every servlet uses to receive orders and send replies.
epj-c2-t03.example: HelloServlet extends HttpServlet, reads request.getParameter("name") and writes a greeting using response.getWriter().
keyPoints: HttpServletRequest: getParameter, getParameterValues, getHeader, getSession, getRequestDispatcher.
HttpServletResponse: setContentType, getWriter, sendRedirect, addCookie, setStatus.
Other: ServletConfig, ServletContext, RequestDispatcher, HttpSession, Cookie.
Newer Tomcat 10+/Jakarta EE 9+ uses package jakarta.servlet instead of javax.servlet.
Servlet API JAR is provided by the container.
commonMistakes: Mixing javax and jakarta imports with the wrong Tomcat.

examQuestions.question: Explain Servlet API hierarchy and main interfaces.
examQuestions.answer: Servlet, GenericServlet, HttpServlet; request/response methods.

examQuestions.question: Write a servlet that greets a user by name.
examQuestions.answer: getParameter + getWriter.

knowledgeCheck.question: Class commonly extended for HTTP servlets:
Method to read a form field?
GenericServlet vs HttpServlet.
knowledgeCheck.answer: GenericServlet is protocol independent; HttpServlet adds HTTP-specific methods.

epj-c2-t03.quickRevision: Servlet API: Servlet → GenericServlet → HttpServlet; request.getParameter, response.getWriter/sendRedirect; javax vs jakarta.
epj-c2-t03.syntax: protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res) throws ServletException, IOException
epj-c2-t03.codeExplanation: getParameter reads the query value; setContentType declares HTML; getWriter writes the response body.
commonErrors: Null from getParameter when the name is misspelled.

epj-c2-t04.title: HTTP Servlets with XML and Annotation
epj-c2-t04.definition: A servlet can be mapped to a URL either in web.xml (<servlet> and <servlet-mapping>) or with the @WebServlet annotation (Servlet 3.0+).
epj-c2-t04.simpleExplanation: Servlet ko URL se map karne ke do tareeke: web.xml (XML configuration) ya @WebServlet annotation (seedha class par).
epj-c2-t04.realLifeAnalogy: Two ways to register a shop: file a paper form (XML) or put a signboard on the shop itself (annotation).
keyPoints: XML mapping uses servlet-name to link <servlet> and <servlet-mapping>.
Annotations need Servlet 3.0+ and metadata-complete not true.
web.xml settings override annotations when both exist.
Annotation: less boilerplate; XML: central configuration without recompiling.

examQuestions.question: Map a servlet using web.xml and annotation.
examQuestions.answer: Show XML and @WebServlet versions.

examQuestions.question: web.xml vs annotation.
examQuestions.answer: XML central, changeable without recompiling, overrides; annotation inline, concise.

knowledgeCheck.question: Two servlets map the same URL. Result?
Exact vs wildcard pattern.
knowledgeCheck.answer: /hello matches only that path; /api/* matches anything under /api.

epj-c2-t04.quickRevision: Mapping: web.xml (<servlet>+<servlet-mapping>) or @WebServlet; XML overrides annotation; patterns exact/path/extension.
epj-c2-t04.code:
<!-- web.xml -->
<servlet>
  <servlet-name>hello</servlet-name>
  <servlet-class>com.demo.HelloServlet</servlet-class>
</servlet>
<servlet-mapping>
  <servlet-name>hello</servlet-name>
  <url-pattern>/hello</url-pattern>
</servlet-mapping>

// Annotation alternative
@WebServlet("/hello")
public class HelloServlet extends HttpServlet { … }
epj-c2-t04.codeExplanation: Both approaches register the same servlet for /hello; use one, not both.

epj-c2-t05.title: Servlets Configuration
epj-c2-t05.definition: ServletConfig holds configuration parameters for one servlet, defined with <init-param> or @WebInitParam and read in init().
epj-c2-t05.simpleExplanation: ServletConfig ek servlet ke liye alag settings deta hai (init parameters), jaise DB url. Har servlet ka apna ServletConfig hota hai.
epj-c2-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A personal instruction sheet given to one employee.
commonMistakes: Expecting init-param visible to other servlets.

examQuestions.question: Use ServletConfig to read an init parameter.
examQuestions.answer: Declare init-param; getInitParameter.

examQuestions.question: ServletConfig vs ServletContext.
examQuestions.answer: Config: per servlet; context: per web app.

knowledgeCheck.question: Each servlet needs its own DB table name. Use?
init-param vs context-param.
knowledgeCheck.answer: init-param per servlet; context-param for the whole app.

epj-c2-t05.codeExplanation: initParams provides a value for this servlet only; getInitParameter retrieves it.
commonErrors: Null result due to wrong param name.

epj-c2-t06.title: Servlets Context
epj-c2-t06.definition: ServletContext is a single object per web application shared by all servlets, giving access to context parameters, attributes, resources and server information.
epj-c2-t06.simpleExplanation: ServletContext poore web app ke liye ek hota hai. Sab servlets shared data (attributes) aur context-params use kar sakte hain.
epj-c2-t06.realLifeAnalogy: A notice board in the school office visible to every teacher (servlet).
epj-c2-t06.example: web.xml <context-param> dbName=college; any servlet reads getServletContext().getInitParameter("dbName"). Counter stored with setAttribute("hits", n).
keyPoints: One ServletContext per web application per JVM.
Other methods: getRealPath, getContextPath, getResourceAsStream, log().
Attributes are not thread-safe without synchronisation.

examQuestions.question: ServletConfig vs ServletContext.
examQuestions.answer: Config per servlet and init-param; context per application with context-param and shared attributes.

examQuestions.question: Share a hit counter via ServletContext.
examQuestions.answer: getAttribute/setAttribute in servlet.

knowledgeCheck.question: Context attributes are shared across servlets.
Share DB name across all servlets. Use?
Request vs context attribute scope.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Request: one request; context: entire application.

epj-c2-t06.quickRevision: ServletContext: one per app; context-params, attributes (shared), getRealPath; sync needed.
epj-c2-t06.expectedOutput: Hits: 1, then Hits: 2 on the next request
epj-c2-t06.codeExplanation: The counter lives in the context so every servlet and request sees the same value.
commonErrors: Race conditions when updating shared attributes.

epj-c2-t07.title: Servlets Collaboration
epj-c2-t07.definition: Servlet collaboration is communication between servlets using RequestDispatcher (forward, include), sendRedirect and shared attributes.
epj-c2-t07.simpleExplanation: Servlets aapas me milke kaam karte hain: forward (control doosre servlet ko, same request), include (doosre ka output add), sendRedirect (browser ko naye URL par bhejna).
epj-c2-t07.realLifeAnalogy: A reception desk either hands you to another counter inside (forward), asks another counter to add a note (include), or tells you to walk to another building (redirect).
epj-c2-t07.example: LoginServlet validates and forwards to WelcomeServlet using RequestDispatcher; on failure includes an error message and redisplays the form.
keyPoints: forward: server-side, same request/response, URL does not change.
include: output of the other resource is included in the response.
sendRedirect: client-side, new request, URL changes, can go to other sites.
Share data via request.setAttribute (forward/include) or session/context.
After forward, no further output in the original servlet.
commonMistakes: Using forward to an external site (not possible).

examQuestions.question: forward() vs sendRedirect().
examQuestions.answer: Server-side/same request/URL unchanged vs client-side/new request/URL changes.

examQuestions.question: Forward a request from LoginServlet to WelcomeServlet.
examQuestions.answer: RequestDispatcher rd = request.getRequestDispatcher("/welcome"); rd.forward(request,response);

knowledgeCheck.question: forward uses the same request object.
Method to share data in the same request?
include vs forward.
knowledgeCheck.answer: include adds the other resource's output to current response; forward transfers control entirely.

epj-c2-t07.quickRevision: Collaboration: RequestDispatcher forward (same request, URL same), include, sendRedirect (new request, URL changes).
epj-c2-t07.expectedOutput: admin → Welcome admin page; others → redirected to login.html
epj-c2-t07.codeExplanation: Forward keeps the request (with attribute msg) on the server; redirect asks the browser to request login.html.

epj-c2-t08.title: Session Tracking
epj-c2-t08.definition: Session tracking maintains user state across multiple HTTP requests using cookies, hidden form fields, URL rewriting or the HttpSession API.
epj-c2-t08.simpleExplanation: HTTP stateless hai, isliye server ko yaad nahi rehta ki aap kaun ho. Session tracking se user ki state yaad rakhte hain: cookies, hidden fields, URL rewriting, ya HttpSession.
epj-c2-t08.realLifeAnalogy: A cloakroom token: the server gives you a token (session ID) and recognises you every time you show it.
epj-c2-t08.example: After login, store the username in the HttpSession; the next servlet reads session.getAttribute("user") to greet the user.
keyPoints: Techniques: Cookies, Hidden form fields, URL rewriting, HttpSession.
HttpSession: server-side data keyed by JSESSIONID cookie.
Methods: getSession(), setAttribute, getAttribute, invalidate(), setMaxInactiveInterval().
Cookie: small data stored in browser; use new Cookie(name,value), response.addCookie.
URL rewriting works if cookies are disabled: response.encodeURL().

examQuestions.question: Explain session tracking techniques.
examQuestions.answer: Cookies, hidden fields, URL rewriting, HttpSession.

examQuestions.question: Cookie vs HttpSession.
examQuestions.answer: Cookie stored on client (size limited, visible); session stored on server with ID cookie.

knowledgeCheck.question: Hidden field vs URL rewriting.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Hidden fields travel in forms; URL rewriting appends session ID to links.

epj-c2-t08.quickRevision: Session tracking: cookies, hidden fields, URL rewriting, HttpSession (JSESSIONID); invalidate on logout.
epj-c2-t08.codeExplanation: The session object persists between requests; getSession(false) avoids creating a new session.

epj-c2-t09.title: CRUD Operations (Servlets)
epj-c2-t09.definition: CRUD operations in servlets use Create, Read, Update and Delete actions mapped to SQL INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE through JDBC, usually via a DAO class.
epj-c2-t09.simpleExplanation: CRUD matlab Create, Read, Update, Delete. Servlet form data leta hai, JDBC PreparedStatement se database me INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE karta hai aur result dikhata hai.
epj-c2-t09.realLifeAnalogy: A library desk: add a book (create), look up (read), correct details (update) and remove old books (delete).
epj-c2-t09.example: StudentServlet with action parameter: add → INSERT; list → SELECT; update → UPDATE; delete → DELETE using PreparedStatement.
keyPoints: Create: INSERT; Read: SELECT; Update: UPDATE; Delete: DELETE.
Use doPost for create/update/delete and doGet for read.
DAO pattern separates database code from servlet.
Use PreparedStatement to avoid SQL injection.
Redirect after POST to avoid duplicate submission.

examQuestions.question: Write servlet code for inserting a student.
examQuestions.answer: PreparedStatement INSERT in doPost.

examQuestions.question: Why redirect after POST?
examQuestions.answer: To prevent form resubmission on refresh (PRG pattern).

knowledgeCheck.question: DAO separates DB code from servlet.
Delete student with id from request. Safe approach?
doGet vs doPost for create.
knowledgeCheck.answer: doPost is preferred for changes; doGet for reads.

epj-c2-t09.quickRevision: CRUD in servlets: INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE via JDBC PreparedStatement; DAO; PRG redirect.
epj-c2-t09.syntax: PreparedStatement ps = con.prepareStatement("INSERT INTO student(id,name) VALUES(?,?)");
epj-c2-t09.expectedOutput: Form add id=3,name=Meena → row inserted → redirect to list
epj-c2-t09.codeExplanation: The action parameter selects the operation; PreparedStatement binds values; redirect avoids duplicate submits.

epj-c3-t01.title: Scripting Elements
epj-c3-t01.definition: JSP scripting elements embed Java code in a JSP page: scriptlet <% %>, expression <%= %>, declaration <%! %> and comments <%-- --%>.
epj-c3-t01.simpleExplanation: JSP me HTML ke andar Java code likhne ke 3 tareeke: scriptlet (<% %>) logic ke liye, expression (<%= %>) value print karne ke liye, declaration (<%! %>) variables/methods ke liye.
epj-c3-t01.realLifeAnalogy: A printed letter with blanks: expressions fill a blank with a value, scriptlets are instructions in the margin.
epj-c3-t01.example: <%! int count = 0; %> declares a field; <% count++; %> runs code; <%= count %> prints it; <%-- comment --%> is not sent to the browser.
keyPoints: Expression <%= expr %> is output via out.print() (no semicolon).
JSP is translated to a servlet and compiled on first request.
Implicit objects: request, response, out, session, application, config, pageContext, page, exception.
ifYouKnow: Write a JSP with all elements.
commonMistakes: Using a semicolon in an expression.
Putting logic-heavy code in JSP instead of servlets.

examQuestions.question: Explain JSP scripting elements with examples.
examQuestions.answer: Scriptlet, expression, declaration, comment with code.

examQuestions.question: Scriptlet vs declaration.
examQuestions.answer: Scriptlet goes inside _jspService (local); declaration defines class-level members.

knowledgeCheck.question: JSP is converted into a servlet.
Declare an instance method in JSP. Tag?
JSP comment vs HTML comment.
knowledgeCheck.answer: JSP comment is not sent to the browser; HTML comment is.

epj-c3-t01.quickRevision: JSP scripting: <% scriptlet %>, <%= expression %>, <%! declaration %>; JSP→servlet; 9 implicit objects.
epj-c3-t01.code:
<%! int count = 0; %> <% count++; String name = request.getParameter("name"); %>

Hello <%= (name == null) ? "Guest" : name %>

Visits: <%= count %>
epj-c3-t01.codeExplanation: The declaration creates a field, the scriptlet increments it and reads a parameter, the expressions print values.
commonErrors: Count field shared by all users (thread-safety).

epj-c3-t02.title: Directive Elements
epj-c3-t02.definition: JSP directives give instructions to the JSP container at translation time: page, include and taglib.
epj-c3-t02.simpleExplanation: Directive JSP container ko batata hai page ko kaise translate karna hai. Teen types: page (settings), include (file include karna), taglib (tag library).
epj-c3-t02.realLifeAnalogy: Setup instructions at the top of a document: paper size, headers to attach, extra fonts to load.
epj-c3-t02.example: <%@ page import="java.util.*" contentType="text/html" errorPage="error.jsp" %>; <%@ include file="header.jsp" %>; <%@ taglib prefix="c" uri="http://java.sun.com/jsp/jstl/core" %>.
keyPoints: page attributes: import, contentType, language, session, errorPage, isErrorPage, buffer.
include directive: static inclusion at translation time (file merged before compile).
taglib directive: declares custom/JSTL tag libraries.
jsp:include action is dynamic (at request time).
Directives affect the generated servlet class.

examQuestions.question: include directive vs jsp:include action.
examQuestions.answer: Directive: static, translation time, merged; action: dynamic, request time, output included.

examQuestions.question: Explain JSP directives.
examQuestions.answer: page, include, taglib with syntax.

knowledgeCheck.question: isErrorPage purpose.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Marks a page as an error handler with access to exception object.

epj-c3-t02.quickRevision: Directives <%@ %>: page (import, errorPage), include (static, translation time), taglib; jsp:include is dynamic.
epj-c3-t02.code:
<%@ page import="java.util.Date" contentType="text/html" errorPage="error.jsp" %> <%@ include file="header.jsp" %>

Today: <%= new Date() %>
epj-c3-t02.expectedOutput: Header content followed by Today: <current date>
epj-c3-t02.codeExplanation: page imports Date and sets the error page; the include directive merges header.jsp before compilation.
commonErrors: Missing import causing compile error in generated servlet.
Wrong relative path in include file.

epj-c3-t03.title: CRUD Operations (JSP)
epj-c3-t03.definition: CRUD in JSP uses forms that submit to JSP/servlet code which performs INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE with JDBC and displays the results.
epj-c3-t03.simpleExplanation: JSP me form se data jata hai, JDBC se database me insert/select/update/delete hota hai, aur list table me dikhaya jata hai. Best practice: logic servlet/DAO me, JSP sirf display.
epj-c3-t03.realLifeAnalogy: A data-entry counter: forms to add, a list to view, and buttons to edit or remove.
epj-c3-t03.example: register.jsp form → insert.jsp executes INSERT → list.jsp loops over ResultSet and prints a table with Edit/Delete links.
keyPoints: Better design: servlet controller + DAO + JSP view (MVC).
Close connections and redirect after changes.
commonMistakes: Writing heavy JDBC code inside JSP.

examQuestions.question: Write JSP code to insert and list records.
examQuestions.answer: Form + JDBC INSERT + SELECT loop.

examQuestions.question: Why avoid JDBC in JSP?
examQuestions.answer: Mixes presentation with logic; use servlet/DAO instead.

knowledgeCheck.question: JSP form submission method for insert:
JSTL can replace scriptlets for loops.
JSP vs servlet in CRUD.
knowledgeCheck.answer: JSP for view; servlet for controller logic.

epj-c3-t03.quickRevision: JSP CRUD: form → JDBC (PreparedStatement) → table; use servlet+DAO for logic and JSP for view.
epj-c3-t03.code:
<%@ page import="java.sql.*" %>
<%
  String name = request.getParameter("name");
  try (Connection c = DriverManager.getConnection("jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/college","root","root");
       PreparedStatement p = c.prepareStatement("INSERT INTO student(name) VALUES(?)")) {
    p.setString(1, name);
    out.println(p.executeUpdate() + " row inserted");
  }
%>
epj-c3-t03.codeExplanation: The scriptlet reads the form field and runs a parameterised INSERT; out prints the result.
commonErrors: NullPointerException when the form field is missing.

epj-c4-t01.title: Hibernate Architecture
epj-c4-t01.definition: Hibernate is an ORM framework whose architecture consists of Configuration, SessionFactory, Session, Transaction and Query objects built on top of JDBC and a database.
epj-c4-t01.simpleExplanation: Hibernate ek ORM framework hai jo Java objects ko database tables se map karta hai. Architecture: Configuration → SessionFactory (ek baar) → Session (har kaam ke liye) → Transaction → Query → JDBC → Database.
epj-c4-t01.realLifeAnalogy: A translator between Java objects and database tables, so you write objects and it writes SQL.
epj-c4-t01.example: Configuration reads hibernate.cfg.xml; builds SessionFactory once; each unit of work opens a Session, begins a Transaction, saves a Student object, commits.
keyPoints: SessionFactory: heavyweight, thread-safe, one per database.
Session: lightweight, not thread-safe; represents a unit of work; first-level cache.
Uses JDBC, JTA and JNDI underneath.

examQuestions.question: Explain Hibernate architecture with a diagram.
examQuestions.answer: Application → Configuration/SessionFactory/Session/Transaction/Query → JDBC → DB.

examQuestions.question: SessionFactory vs Session.
examQuestions.answer: SessionFactory: heavy, one per app, thread-safe; Session: light, per unit of work, not thread-safe.

knowledgeCheck.question: One SessionFactory per request. Problem?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Very expensive; should be one per app.

knowledgeCheck.question: ORM vs JDBC.
knowledgeCheck.answer: ORM maps objects to tables and generates SQL; JDBC needs manual SQL and mapping.

epj-c4-t01.quickRevision: Hibernate: Configuration → SessionFactory (1, heavy, thread-safe) → Session (light, not thread-safe) → Transaction → Query → JDBC → DB.
epj-c4-t01.syntax:
SessionFactory sf = new Configuration().configure().buildSessionFactory();
Session s = sf.openSession();
epj-c4-t01.expectedOutput: Hibernate: insert into student (name, id) values (?, ?)
epj-c4-t01.codeExplanation: The factory is built once; each session wraps a transaction; persist schedules an INSERT executed at commit.

epj-c4-t02.title: JPA
epj-c4-t02.definition: JPA (Java/Jakarta Persistence API) is the standard specification for ORM in Java; Hibernate is its most popular implementation.
epj-c4-t02.simpleExplanation: JPA ek standard (specification) hai ORM ke liye; Hibernate uska implementation hai. JPA annotations (@Entity, @Id) aur EntityManager use karte hain, jisse code provider se independent hota hai.
epj-c4-t02.realLifeAnalogy: JPA is the rulebook; Hibernate is a team that plays by those rules.
epj-c4-t02.example: @Entity class Student with @Id; persistence.xml defines persistence-unit; EntityManager em.persist(student) inside a transaction.
ifYouKnow: Explain JPA and its relation to Hibernate.
commonMistakes: Thinking JPA is a framework (it is a specification).

examQuestions.question: JPA vs Hibernate.
examQuestions.answer: JPA: specification; Hibernate: implementation with extra native features.

examQuestions.question: Which object replaces Session in JPA?
examQuestions.answer: EntityManager.

knowledgeCheck.question: Switch ORM provider without code changes. Use?
Session vs EntityManager.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Session is Hibernate-native; EntityManager is the JPA standard equivalent.

epj-c4-t02.quickRevision: JPA: ORM spec (javax/jakarta.persistence); Hibernate implements; EntityManager, persistence.xml, JPQL.
epj-c4-t02.codeExplanation: Persistence.createEntityManagerFactory reads persistence.xml; persist plus commit stores the entity.
commonErrors: No Persistence provider for EntityManager named myPU.

epj-c4-t03.title: Generator Class
epj-c4-t03.definition: A generator class (identifier generation strategy) tells Hibernate how to produce primary key values for entities, such as assigned, increment, identity, sequence, native or UUID.
epj-c4-t03.simpleExplanation: Generator class primary key kaise banegi ye batati hai: khud assign karo, auto-increment (identity), sequence, ya UUID. Annotation: @GeneratedValue(strategy=...).
epj-c4-t03.realLifeAnalogy: A ticket machine that issues the next token number automatically.
epj-c4-t03.example: @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY) private int id; → MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT. XML: <generator class="native"/>.
keyPoints: native: picks identity/sequence by dialect; uuid: generates a UUID.
JPA GenerationType: AUTO, IDENTITY, SEQUENCE, TABLE.

examQuestions.question: Explain Hibernate generator classes.
examQuestions.answer: List strategies and use cases.

examQuestions.question: identity vs sequence.
examQuestions.answer: Identity uses auto-increment column; sequence uses a database sequence object.

knowledgeCheck.question: assigned means application provides the id.
Oracle DB needs generated ids. Strategy?
native vs assigned.
knowledgeCheck.answer: native lets DB/dialect choose; assigned requires manual id.

epj-c4-t03.quickRevision: Generators: assigned, increment, identity (MySQL), sequence (Oracle/PG), native, uuid; @GeneratedValue(strategy=…).
epj-c4-t03.expectedOutput: insert into Student (name) values (?)  -- id generated by the database
epj-c4-t03.codeExplanation: IDENTITY leaves the id column out of INSERT; MySQL assigns the next number.
commonErrors: Manually setting an id on a generated entity.

epj-c4-t04.title: Dialects
epj-c4-t04.definition: A Hibernate dialect is a class that tells Hibernate which SQL variant to generate for a particular database.
epj-c4-t04.simpleExplanation: Har database ka SQL thoda alag hota hai (LIMIT vs ROWNUM). Dialect Hibernate ko batata hai ki kaunsa DB hai taaki sahi SQL generate ho. Config: hibernate.dialect.
epj-c4-t04.realLifeAnalogy: Choosing the right language dialect so the translator speaks the way the local people do.
keyPoints: Examples: MySQLDialect/MySQL8Dialect, Oracle dialects, PostgreSQLDialect, SQLServerDialect.
Controls data type mapping, pagination, functions and id generation.
Wrong dialect gives SQL syntax errors.
Switching DB = change dialect + driver + URL.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to update dialect when switching DB.

examQuestions.question: What is a dialect in Hibernate?
examQuestions.answer: Class mapping Hibernate SQL generation to a specific DB; property hibernate.dialect.

examQuestions.question: What changes when moving MySQL to Oracle?
examQuestions.answer: Driver, URL, dialect, and possibly id strategy.

knowledgeCheck.question: Syntax error near LIMIT on Oracle. Cause?
Dialect vs driver.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Driver connects; dialect shapes the SQL.

epj-c4-t04.quickRevision: Dialect: hibernate.dialect tells Hibernate DB-specific SQL (pagination, types); change with the DB.
epj-c4-t04.codeExplanation: The dialect, driver and URL together define how Hibernate talks to MySQL.

epj-c4-t05.title: Mapping
epj-c4-t05.definition: Mapping in Hibernate defines how Java classes and their relationships correspond to database tables, using XML (hbm) or annotations, including one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many associations.
epj-c4-t05.simpleExplanation: Mapping batata hai class → table, field → column, aur objects ke beech relationships (one-to-many etc.). XML ya annotations se kiya jata hai.
epj-c4-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A translation table between a class diagram and a database diagram.
epj-c4-t05.example: Department 1—* Employee: Employee has @ManyToOne @JoinColumn(name="dept_id") Department dept; Department has @OneToMany(mappedBy="dept") List<Employee> employees.
keyPoints: @JoinColumn defines foreign key; mappedBy marks the inverse side.
cascade = persist/remove propagation; fetch = LAZY or EAGER.

examQuestions.question: Explain mapping and association types in Hibernate.
examQuestions.answer: Class-table mapping and four associations with examples.

examQuestions.question: Lazy vs eager fetching.
examQuestions.answer: Lazy loads related data on access; eager loads immediately with the owner.

knowledgeCheck.question: LazyInitializationException. Cause?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Accessing a lazy collection after the session closed.

knowledgeCheck.question: XML vs annotation mapping.
knowledgeCheck.answer: XML external config; annotations inline in classes.

epj-c4-t05.codeExplanation: The ManyToOne side owns the foreign key; mappedBy on the OneToMany side points to that field.
commonErrors: Infinite recursion in toString/JSON with bidirectional links.
Missing cascade so child not saved.

epj-c4-t06.title: Annotations
epj-c4-t06.definition: Hibernate/JPA annotations declare mapping metadata directly in the entity class, such as @Entity, @Table, @Id, @Column, @GeneratedValue and @Transient.
epj-c4-t06.simpleExplanation: Annotations se XML ke bina class me hi mapping likh dete hain: @Entity (table banao), @Id (primary key), @Column (column settings), @Transient (store mat karo).
epj-c4-t06.realLifeAnalogy: Sticky labels on a form that tell the system how each field is stored.
epj-c4-t06.example: @Entity @Table(name="student") class Student { @Id @GeneratedValue int id; @Column(name="full_name", nullable=false, length=50) String name; @Transient int age; }
keyPoints: @Entity marks a persistent class; @Table sets table name.
@Transient excludes a field; @Temporal for dates; @Enumerated for enums; @Lob for large data.

examQuestions.question: Write an annotated Student entity.
examQuestions.answer: Show @Entity, @Id, @Column, @Transient.

examQuestions.question: What does @Transient do?
examQuestions.answer: The field is not persisted.

knowledgeCheck.question: Column name differs from field name. Use?
@Table vs @Entity.
knowledgeCheck.answer: @Entity marks a persistent class; @Table configures its table name/schema.

epj-c4-t06.expectedOutput: Table student(id, full_name) — age not stored
epj-c4-t06.codeExplanation: Annotations define table, key, column rules and exclude age from persistence.

epj-c4-t07.title: Transaction Management
epj-c4-t07.definition: Transaction management in Hibernate groups database operations into an atomic unit using Transaction begin, commit and rollback to maintain ACID properties.
epj-c4-t07.simpleExplanation: Transaction me kai operations ek unit ki tarah hote hain: ya sab commit, ya koi error aaye to rollback. Hibernate me session.beginTransaction(), commit(), rollback().
epj-c4-t07.realLifeAnalogy: Bank transfer: both debit and credit must succeed together or neither should happen.
epj-c4-t07.example: Debit account A and credit account B inside one transaction; if the credit throws an exception, rollback restores A.
keyPoints: Pattern: try { … commit } catch { rollback } finally { close }.
Isolation levels: read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable.
Reads also need a transaction for consistency; one transaction per unit of work.

examQuestions.question: Write Hibernate code with commit and rollback.
examQuestions.answer: try/catch pattern.

examQuestions.question: Explain ACID.
examQuestions.answer: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability with bank example.

knowledgeCheck.question: JTA vs local transaction.
knowledgeCheck.answer: JTA is container-managed across resources; local is per connection.

epj-c4-t07.quickRevision: Transactions: begin → commit / rollback; ACID; try-catch-finally; JTA vs local.
epj-c4-t07.expectedOutput: Committed on success; rollback and stack trace on failure
epj-c4-t07.codeExplanation: Rollback in catch prevents partial changes; finally always closes the session.

epj-c4-t08.title: HQL
epj-c4-t08.definition: HQL (Hibernate Query Language) is an object-oriented query language that queries entity classes and their properties instead of tables and columns.
epj-c4-t08.simpleExplanation: HQL SQL jaisi hai par tables ki jagah classes aur properties use hoti hain: 'from Student where name = :n'. Hibernate ise SQL me convert karta hai.
epj-c4-t08.realLifeAnalogy: SQL but speaking in object names (Student) instead of table names (student_tbl).
epj-c4-t08.example: Query q = session.createQuery("from Student s where s.name = :n"); q.setParameter("n", "Asha"); List<Student> list = q.list();
keyPoints: Uses entity class and property names (case-sensitive).
Supports select, from, where, order by, group by, joins, aggregates.
commonMistakes: Using table/column names instead of class/property names.

examQuestions.question: Write HQL to fetch students with marks > 60 ordered by name.
examQuestions.answer: from Student s where s.marks > 60 order by s.name.

examQuestions.question: HQL vs SQL.
examQuestions.answer: HQL queries objects/properties and is DB independent; SQL queries tables/columns.

knowledgeCheck.question: list() vs uniqueResult().
knowledgeCheck.answer: list returns many; uniqueResult returns one or null.

epj-c4-t08.quickRevision: HQL: object-oriented queries (from Student where …); :named params; setFirstResult/setMaxResults; executeUpdate for bulk.
epj-c4-t08.syntax: Query<Student> q = session.createQuery("from Student where marks > :m", Student.class);
epj-c4-t08.codeExplanation: Named parameter :m avoids injection; paging limits rows; entity names not table names.
commonErrors: QuerySyntaxException: Student is not mapped (wrong entity name).

epj-c4-t09.title: HCQL
epj-c4-t09.definition: HCQL (Hibernate Criteria Query Language) builds queries programmatically with the Criteria API using restrictions, ordering and projections instead of query strings.
epj-c4-t09.simpleExplanation: HCQL me query string nahi likhte; Java objects/methods se query banate hain (Restrictions.eq, gt, like). Compile-time safe aur dynamic queries ke liye achha. Note: legacy Criteria deprecated; JPA CriteriaBuilder use hota hai.
epj-c4-t09.realLifeAnalogy: Building a query by clicking filter buttons instead of typing a sentence.
keyPoints: Criteria API: programmatic, type-safe, good for dynamic filters.
Legacy Hibernate Criteria is deprecated (5.2) and removed (6); use JPA Criteria.

examQuestions.question: Write HCQL to fetch students with marks > 60.
examQuestions.answer: Legacy and JPA CriteriaBuilder versions.

examQuestions.question: HQL vs HCQL.
examQuestions.answer: HQL string-based; HCQL object-based, good for dynamic queries.

knowledgeCheck.question: Restrictions vs Projections.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Restrictions filter rows; projections choose columns/aggregates.

epj-c4-t09.quickRevision: HCQL: Criteria API with Restrictions/Order/Projections; legacy removed in Hibernate 6 → JPA CriteriaBuilder.
epj-c4-t09.syntax: CriteriaBuilder cb = session.getCriteriaBuilder(); CriteriaQuery<Student> cq = cb.createQuery(Student.class);
epj-c4-t09.expectedOutput: Students with marks > 60 ordered by name
epj-c4-t09.codeExplanation: Criteria objects represent select, where and order parts without writing HQL strings.

epj-c4-t10.title: CRUD Operations (Hibernate)
epj-c4-t10.definition: Hibernate CRUD operations use Session methods: persist/save (create), get/load (read), update/merge (update) and delete/remove (delete), each inside a transaction.
epj-c4-t10.simpleExplanation: Hibernate CRUD: save/persist se insert, get/load se read, update/merge se modify, delete/remove se delete — sab transaction ke andar.
epj-c4-t10.realLifeAnalogy: Add a book card, look it up, correct it and throw it away, all through a librarian (Session).
epj-c4-t10.example: Create Student(1,'Asha'); read with session.get(Student.class,1); change name and merge; delete with session.remove(s).
keyPoints: Read: get() (returns null if missing, hits DB immediately) / load() (proxy, throws ObjectNotFoundException later).
Update: modify a persistent object (dirty checking) or merge()/update().
commonMistakes: Using load() and accessing after session close (LazyInitializationException).

examQuestions.question: Write Hibernate code for CRUD on Student.
examQuestions.answer: Persist, get, modify, remove in transactions.

examQuestions.question: get() vs load().
examQuestions.answer: get hits DB and returns null; load returns proxy and throws if missing on access.

knowledgeCheck.question: Persistent object changes are saved at commit (dirty checking).
save vs persist.
knowledgeCheck.answer: save returns the id (Hibernate-specific); persist is JPA, returns void.

epj-c4-t10.quickRevision: Hibernate CRUD: persist/save, get/load, modify+commit or merge, remove/delete; get returns null, load proxy.
epj-c4-t10.expectedOutput: insert → select → update → delete statements in the SQL log
epj-c4-t10.codeExplanation: All four operations run in one transaction; the update is detected automatically before commit.
commonErrors: NonUniqueObjectException with two instances of same id.

epj-c5-t01.title: Spring Architecture
epj-c5-t01.definition: The Spring Framework is a modular Java framework built around an Inversion of Control (IoC) container, with layers for core container, AOP, data access/integration, web and test.
epj-c5-t01.simpleExplanation: Spring ek lightweight framework hai jo objects (beans) ko khud create aur manage karta hai (IoC). Architecture layers: Core Container, AOP, Data Access, Web, Test.
epj-c5-t01.realLifeAnalogy: A building with a central management office (IoC container) that hires and supplies staff (beans) to each department.
epj-c5-t01.example: Application asks the ApplicationContext for a bean; the container creates it, injects its dependencies and returns it.
keyPoints: Core Container: Core, Beans, Context, SpEL.
AOP and Aspects: cross-cutting concerns (logging, transactions).
Data Access/Integration: JDBC, ORM, JMS, Transactions.
IoC container manages bean lifecycle and dependency injection.
commonMistakes: Thinking Spring is only for web applications.
Confusing IoC with DI (DI implements IoC).

examQuestions.question: Explain the architecture of Spring Framework.
examQuestions.answer: Core container, AOP, data access, web, test layers with IoC.

examQuestions.question: What is IoC?
examQuestions.answer: Control of object creation and wiring is given to the container instead of the application.

knowledgeCheck.question: IoC vs DI.
knowledgeCheck.answer: IoC is the principle; DI is a way to implement it.

epj-c5-t01.quickRevision: Spring: IoC container + modules (Core, AOP, Data Access, Web, Test); beans managed by container.
epj-c5-t01.syntax:
ApplicationContext ctx = new ClassPathXmlApplicationContext("beans.xml");
Car c = ctx.getBean("car", Car.class);
epj-c5-t01.codeExplanation: The container reads configuration, creates the greeting bean and returns it.

epj-c5-t02.title: Spring Modules
epj-c5-t02.definition: Spring is divided into modules such as Core, Beans, Context, SpEL, AOP, JDBC, ORM, Transactions, JMS, Web, Web MVC and Test, which can be used independently.
epj-c5-t02.simpleExplanation: Spring ke modules alag-alag kaam sambhalte hain: Core/Beans (IoC), Context (ApplicationContext), AOP, JDBC/ORM/Tx (data), Web MVC, Test. Jo chahiye wahi use karo.
epj-c5-t02.realLifeAnalogy: A toolbox with separate drawers: use only the tools needed.
epj-c5-t02.example: A web app uses spring-webmvc (controllers), spring-jdbc (JdbcTemplate) and spring-tx (transactions).
commonMistakes: Pulling the whole framework when only DI is needed.
Confusing Spring modules with Spring projects.

examQuestions.question: Explain Spring modules.
examQuestions.answer: Group by layer with one-line functions.

examQuestions.question: Which module provides JdbcTemplate?
examQuestions.answer: spring-jdbc.

knowledgeCheck.question: Spring Framework vs Spring Boot.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Framework provides the core; Boot adds auto-configuration and starters.

epj-c5-t02.quickRevision: Modules: core/beans/context/spel, aop, jdbc/orm/tx/jms, web/webmvc/websocket, test.

epj-c5-t03.title: Dependency Injection
epj-c5-t03.definition: Dependency Injection (DI) is a pattern where the container supplies an object's dependencies from outside (via constructor, setter or field) instead of the object creating them.
epj-c5-t03.simpleExplanation: DI me class apne dependent objects khud nahi banati; Spring unhe bahar se inject karta hai (constructor, setter ya field). Isse loose coupling aur testing aasan hoti hai.
epj-c5-t03.realLifeAnalogy: A chef who is handed ingredients instead of going to buy them: the cook focuses on cooking.
epj-c5-t03.example: Car depends on Engine. Instead of new Engine() inside Car, Spring creates Engine and injects it into Car through constructor injection (XML ref or @Autowired).
keyPoints: Types: constructor injection, setter injection, (field injection).
XML: <bean id class> with <constructor-arg> or <property ref>.
Benefits: loose coupling, easy testing, reusability.
commonMistakes: Using new inside the class and also injecting.

examQuestions.question: Show constructor and setter injection.
examQuestions.answer: XML beans with constructor-arg and property.

examQuestions.question: Constructor vs setter injection.
examQuestions.answer: Constructor: mandatory, immutable; setter: optional, changeable.

knowledgeCheck.question: Switch Engine implementation without changing Car. Pattern?
DI vs service locator.
knowledgeCheck.answer: DI pushes dependencies in; locator pulls them from a registry.

epj-c5-t03.quickRevision: DI: container injects dependencies (constructor/setter/field) → loose coupling, testable.
epj-c5-t03.codeExplanation: Spring builds engine, then passes it to Car's constructor; Car never calls new Engine().

epj-c5-t04.title: Autowire
epj-c5-t04.definition: Autowiring lets Spring automatically resolve and inject bean dependencies, by type, name or constructor, using @Autowired or XML autowire modes.
epj-c5-t04.simpleExplanation: Autowire Spring ko khud decide karne deta hai kaunsa bean inject karna hai. @Autowired type ke basis par inject karta hai; do beans milen to @Qualifier ya @Primary use karte hain.
epj-c5-t04.realLifeAnalogy: Auto-assigning the right helper to each task without naming them one by one.
epj-c5-t04.example: @Autowired private Engine engine; If there are two Engine beans, use @Qualifier("petrolEngine") or mark one @Primary.
keyPoints: XML modes: no, byName, byType, constructor.
@Autowired by type; works on constructor, setter and field.
commonMistakes: NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException due to two beans of same type.
Using field injection making tests harder.

examQuestions.question: Explain autowiring modes.
examQuestions.answer: no, byName, byType, constructor and annotation approach.

examQuestions.question: Resolve ambiguity with @Qualifier.
examQuestions.answer: Two Engine beans; qualify by name.

knowledgeCheck.question: Two beans of same type, one is default. Use?
@Autowired vs @Resource.
knowledgeCheck.answer: @Autowired by type first; @Resource by name first.

epj-c5-t04.quickRevision: Autowire: byType via @Autowired; ambiguity → @Qualifier/@Primary; XML modes no/byName/byType/constructor.
epj-c5-t04.codeExplanation: Two Engine beans exist; @Qualifier selects the petrol one to avoid ambiguity.

epj-c5-t05.title: Application Context
epj-c5-t05.definition: ApplicationContext is the central Spring interface that represents the IoC container, creating and wiring beans and providing extra features like events, i18n and resource loading.
epj-c5-t05.simpleExplanation: ApplicationContext Spring container hai: beans banata hai, wire karta hai, events aur messages sambhalta hai. BeanFactory se zyada powerful hai.
epj-c5-t05.realLifeAnalogy: The head office that creates all departments, connects them and keeps records.
epj-c5-t05.example: ApplicationContext ctx = new AnnotationConfigApplicationContext(AppConfig.class); Car c = ctx.getBean(Car.class);
keyPoints: Extends BeanFactory; adds events, i18n, resource loading, annotation support.
BeanFactory is lazy; ApplicationContext eagerly instantiates singleton beans.
Bean scopes: singleton (default), prototype, request, session.
commonMistakes: Calling getBean everywhere instead of using DI.
Confusing singleton scope with the singleton pattern (per container).

examQuestions.question: BeanFactory vs ApplicationContext.
examQuestions.answer: BeanFactory basic lazy; ApplicationContext adds events, i18n, eager singleton init, AOP.

examQuestions.question: Explain bean scopes.
examQuestions.answer: singleton, prototype, request, session, application.

knowledgeCheck.question: New instance on every getBean. Scope?
Eager vs lazy.
knowledgeCheck.answer: ApplicationContext eagerly creates singletons; BeanFactory creates on demand.

epj-c5-t05.quickRevision: ApplicationContext: IoC container (extends BeanFactory); XML/annotation/web implementations; singleton default scope.
epj-c5-t05.codeExplanation: Singleton scope returns the same instance per container; prototype would print false.
commonErrors: Mixing prototype beans into singletons without proxies.

epj-c5-t06.title: Annotation-based Configuration
epj-c5-t06.definition: Annotation-based configuration defines beans and wiring using annotations like @Component, @Service, @Repository, @Configuration, @Bean and @Autowired instead of XML.
epj-c5-t06.simpleExplanation: XML ki jagah annotations se beans define karte hain: @Component/@Service/@Repository class par, @Configuration + @Bean method se, aur @ComponentScan se Spring ko batate hain kaha dhundna hai.
epj-c5-t06.realLifeAnalogy: Name tags on staff members instead of a separate paper register.
epj-c5-t06.example: @Configuration @ComponentScan("com.demo") class AppConfig { } ; @Service class OrderService { @Autowired OrderRepo repo; }
keyPoints: @Configuration class with @Bean methods defines beans in Java.

examQuestions.question: Show annotation-based configuration.
examQuestions.answer: AppConfig with @ComponentScan and @Bean.

examQuestions.question: @Component vs @Bean.
examQuestions.answer: @Component on own classes (auto-detected); @Bean method for explicit creation, e.g. third-party classes.

knowledgeCheck.question: Register a third-party class as bean. Use?

epj-c5-t06.codeExplanation: @Bean registers a Greeting bean; the annotation context loads AppConfig and returns it.
commonErrors: Bean not found because package not scanned.

epj-c5-t07.title: Spring MVC
epj-c5-t07.definition: Spring MVC is a web framework following the Model–View–Controller pattern in which a front controller (DispatcherServlet) routes requests to controllers and renders views.
epj-c5-t07.simpleExplanation: Spring MVC me saari requests DispatcherServlet (front controller) ke paas aati hain. Wo HandlerMapping se controller dhundhta hai, controller Model deta hai, ViewResolver view chunta hai, aur page render hota hai.
epj-c5-t07.realLifeAnalogy: A reception desk (DispatcherServlet) sending each visitor to the right department (controller) and then to a waiting room (view).
epj-c5-t07.example: Request /hello → DispatcherServlet → @Controller method returns "hello" and puts message in Model → InternalResourceViewResolver maps to /WEB-INF/views/hello.jsp.
keyPoints: Flow: Request → DispatcherServlet → HandlerMapping → Controller → ModelAndView → ViewResolver → View → Response.
Model carries data to the view.
ViewResolver converts logical view names to actual pages (JSP/Thymeleaf).
commonMistakes: Returning a view name that doesn't map to a page.

examQuestions.question: Explain the Spring MVC request flow.
examQuestions.answer: DispatcherServlet, HandlerMapping, Controller, ViewResolver, View.

examQuestions.question: Write a simple Spring MVC controller.
examQuestions.answer: @Controller with @GetMapping returning view name and Model attribute.

knowledgeCheck.question: ViewResolver maps logical names to views.

epj-c5-t07.quickRevision: Spring MVC: DispatcherServlet → HandlerMapping → Controller → ModelAndView → ViewResolver → View.
epj-c5-t07.syntax: @Controller public class HelloController { @GetMapping("/hello") public String hello(Model m){ … return "hello"; } }
epj-c5-t07.codeExplanation: The controller adds msg to the model and returns a logical view name resolved by the view resolver.
commonErrors: Handler not found: controller not component-scanned.

epj-c5-t08.title: CRUD Operations (Spring)
epj-c5-t08.definition: CRUD in Spring uses Spring MVC controllers with a DAO/service layer, typically JdbcTemplate or Spring Data, to create, read, update and delete database records.
epj-c5-t08.simpleExplanation: Spring me CRUD: Controller request leta hai, Service/DAO JdbcTemplate se database operations karta hai (update() for insert/update/delete, query() for select).
epj-c5-t08.realLifeAnalogy: A clerk (controller) passing forms to the records office (DAO) which uses a standard form-processing tool (JdbcTemplate).
epj-c5-t08.example: StudentDao uses jdbcTemplate.update("INSERT INTO student(name) VALUES(?)", name) and jdbcTemplate.query("SELECT * FROM student", rowMapper).
keyPoints: Methods: update() for DML, query()/queryForObject() for SELECT.
RowMapper maps a row to an object.
DataSource bean configures the DB connection.

examQuestions.question: CRUD with Spring JdbcTemplate.
examQuestions.answer: DAO methods using update and query with RowMapper.

examQuestions.question: Advantage of JdbcTemplate?
examQuestions.answer: Handles resource management and exceptions, reducing boilerplate.

knowledgeCheck.question: RowMapper converts a row to an object.
Two updates must succeed together. Use?

epj-c5-t08.quickRevision: Spring CRUD: Controller → Service → DAO with JdbcTemplate (update/query/RowMapper); DataSource; @Transactional.
epj-c5-t08.codeExplanation: update returns affected rows; query uses a lambda RowMapper to build Student objects.

epj-c6-t01.title: Dependency Injection (Spring Boot)
epj-c6-t01.definition: In Spring Boot, dependency injection works with component scanning and auto-configuration: stereotype beans are detected under the main class package and injected, usually via constructors.
epj-c6-t01.simpleExplanation: Spring Boot me DI wahi hai par setup kam: @SpringBootApplication auto-configuration + component scan karta hai. Beans (@Service, @Repository) apne aap milte hain aur constructor se inject hote hain.
epj-c6-t01.realLifeAnalogy: Same office management, but with a pre-built office layout so you skip the setup.
epj-c6-t01.example: @SpringBootApplication main class; @Service OrderService with constructor taking OrderRepository; Boot finds and injects it automatically.
keyPoints: Scans the main class's package and sub-packages.
commonMistakes: Placing classes outside the main package (not scanned).

examQuestions.question: Explain DI in Spring Boot.
examQuestions.answer: Component scan, auto-config, constructor injection.

examQuestions.question: What does @SpringBootApplication combine?
examQuestions.answer: @Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, @ComponentScan.

knowledgeCheck.question: Single constructor needs no @Autowired in Spring 4.3+.
Bean not found. Check?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Whether it is in the main class's package tree.

knowledgeCheck.question: Spring vs Boot configuration.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Spring needs explicit config; Boot auto-configures by classpath.

epj-c6-t01.quickRevision: Boot DI: @SpringBootApplication (config+autoconfig+scan), constructor injection, application.properties, starters.
epj-c6-t01.syntax: @SpringBootApplication public class App { public static void main(String[] a){ SpringApplication.run(App.class, a);} }
epj-c6-t01.expectedOutput: Application starts; GreetService receives the Greeter bean automatically
epj-c6-t01.codeExplanation: Boot scans the package, creates Greeter and GreetService, and injects through the constructor.
commonErrors: Unsatisfied dependency: bean outside scanned packages.

epj-c6-t02.title: Web App using Spring Boot
epj-c6-t02.definition: A Spring Boot web application uses spring-boot-starter-web, which provides Spring MVC with an embedded server (Tomcat), so it runs as a simple Java application without a separate server.
epj-c6-t02.simpleExplanation: Spring Boot web app me embedded Tomcat milta hai. spring-boot-starter-web add karo, @RestController ya @Controller likho, aur 'mvn spring-boot:run' se app chalao (port 8080).
epj-c6-t02.realLifeAnalogy: A food truck: the kitchen and the stove (server) come built in; you just start cooking.
epj-c6-t02.example: Create project with Spring Initializr (Web dependency). Controller: @GetMapping("/hello") returns "Hello Boot". Run and open http://localhost:8080/hello.
keyPoints: Starter: spring-boot-starter-web (Spring MVC + Jackson + embedded Tomcat).
Run as JAR: java -jar app.jar or mvn spring-boot:run.
Static files in src/main/resources/static; templates in /templates.
commonMistakes: Static files in the wrong folder.

examQuestions.question: Create and run a Spring Boot web app.
examQuestions.answer: Initializr → controller → run → open URL.

examQuestions.question: How change port?
examQuestions.answer: server.port=9090 in application.properties.

knowledgeCheck.question: JAR vs WAR deployment.
knowledgeCheck.answer: JAR runs standalone; WAR deploys to an external container.

epj-c6-t02.quickRevision: Boot web: starter-web (MVC + embedded Tomcat), @RestController/@Controller, run on 8080, server.port to change.
epj-c6-t02.syntax: @RestController public class HelloController { @GetMapping("/hello") String hello(){ return "Hello Boot"; } }
epj-c6-t02.codeExplanation: Starter-web provides MVC and Tomcat; the controller method is mapped to /hello.
commonErrors: Whitelabel Error Page: no mapping found.

epj-c6-t03.title: Spring Boot AOP
epj-c6-t03.definition: Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP) in Spring Boot separates cross-cutting concerns such as logging, security and transactions into aspects applied to methods through pointcuts.
epj-c6-t03.simpleExplanation: AOP me logging, security jaisi common cheezein alag 'aspect' me likhte hain aur pointcut se batate hain kis methods par lagani hain. spring-boot-starter-aop add karo, @Aspect class likho.
epj-c6-t03.realLifeAnalogy: A security guard at the gate who checks everyone entering any room, instead of each room doing its own checks.
epj-c6-t03.example: @Aspect @Component class LogAspect { @Before("execution(* com.demo.service.*.*(..))") void log(JoinPoint jp){ System.out.println("Calling " + jp.getSignature()); } }
keyPoints: Concepts: aspect, advice, join point, pointcut, weaving.
Use for logging, timing, security, transactions.
commonMistakes: Calling an advised method from inside the same class (proxy bypassed).

examQuestions.question: Explain AOP with terms and example.
examQuestions.answer: Aspect, advice, pointcut, join point, weaving; logging aspect.

examQuestions.question: @Before vs @Around.
examQuestions.answer: @Before runs before the method; @Around wraps the call and can control it.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is a pointcut?
knowledgeCheck.answer: An expression selecting join points where advice applies.

knowledgeCheck.question: Log execution time of all service methods. Use?
Aspect vs advice.
knowledgeCheck.answer: Aspect is the module; advice is the action inside it.

epj-c6-t03.codeExplanation: The around advice measures time around proceed(), applying to all service methods without changing them.
commonErrors: Aspect not applied: missing @Component or starter-aop.

epj-c6-t04.title: Spring Boot Database
epj-c6-t04.definition: Spring Boot database support uses spring-boot-starter-data-jpa and a JDBC driver, auto-configures a DataSource from application.properties, and provides repositories (JpaRepository) for CRUD.
epj-c6-t04.simpleExplanation: Spring Boot me database ke liye starter-data-jpa + MySQL driver add karo, application.properties me URL/user/password do, @Entity banao aur JpaRepository extend karo — CRUD methods mil jaate hain.
epj-c6-t04.realLifeAnalogy: A ready-made records clerk: you describe the record type and it gives add/find/delete operations.
epj-c6-t04.example: interface StudentRepo extends JpaRepository<Student,Integer> { List<Student> findByName(String n); } → save(), findAll(), findById(), deleteById() free.
keyPoints: @Entity maps a class; JpaRepository<T,ID> gives CRUD.

examQuestions.question: Spring Boot with MySQL CRUD.
examQuestions.answer: Properties, entity, repository, service.

examQuestions.question: What does JpaRepository provide?
examQuestions.answer: save, findAll, findById, deleteById, count, paging and more.

knowledgeCheck.question: Derived query method names generate SQL.
JdbcTemplate vs JPA repository.
knowledgeCheck.answer: JdbcTemplate: manual SQL; JPA repository: ORM with generated CRUD.

epj-c6-t04.quickRevision: Boot DB: starter-data-jpa + driver; spring.datasource.* props; @Entity + JpaRepository (save/findAll/findById/deleteById); derived queries.
epj-c6-t04.syntax: public interface StudentRepo extends JpaRepository<Student, Integer> {}
epj-c6-t04.expectedOutput: repo.save(new Student("Asha")) inserts; findByName("Asha") returns the row
epj-c6-t04.codeExplanation: Boot creates the DataSource and EntityManager from properties; the repository interface is implemented automatically.

epj-c6-t05.title: Spring Rest
epj-c6-t05.definition: Spring REST builds RESTful web services with @RestController and HTTP-method annotations, exchanging JSON and mapping GET, POST, PUT and DELETE to read, create, update and delete operations.
epj-c6-t05.simpleExplanation: Spring REST me controller JSON return karta hai (@RestController). HTTP methods ke hisaab se CRUD: GET=read, POST=create, PUT=update, DELETE=delete. Postman ya curl se test karte hain.
epj-c6-t05.realLifeAnalogy: A vending machine with fixed buttons: each button (HTTP verb + URL) triggers one standard action and returns a standard response (JSON).
epj-c6-t05.example: GET /students → list; GET /students/1 → one; POST /students (JSON body) → create; PUT /students/1 → update; DELETE /students/1 → remove, returning proper status codes.
keyPoints: @PathVariable reads URL parts; @RequestBody reads JSON; @RequestParam reads query.
REST principles: stateless, resource URLs, uniform interface.

examQuestions.question: Write a REST controller for Student CRUD.
examQuestions.answer: Controller with the four verbs and ResponseEntity.

examQuestions.question: @Controller vs @RestController.
examQuestions.answer: RestController writes return values to the body as JSON.

knowledgeCheck.question: PUT vs POST.
knowledgeCheck.answer: POST creates; PUT replaces/updates an existing resource (idempotent).

epj-c6-t05.quickRevision: REST: @RestController; GET read, POST create, PUT update, DELETE delete; @PathVariable, @RequestBody, ResponseEntity; JSON via Jackson.
epj-c6-t05.expectedOutput: GET /students → [{"id":1,"name":"Asha"}]; POST → 201 with created JSON; DELETE → 204
epj-c6-t05.codeExplanation: Each method handles one verb/URL; ResponseEntity sets the right status; Jackson converts objects to JSON.
commonErrors: 415 Unsupported Media Type: missing Content-Type: application/json.
